_meta.description: Document-rules config for release_deed — Release / Relinquishment deed where a co-sharer or co-owner gives up rights in favour of another. Common in family settlements (especially among heirs releasing share to one sibling). NOTE — Release WITHOUT consideration to non-co-sharer is essentially a GIFT (different stamp duty); release WITH consideration to co-sharer is treated like sale / partition. Registration mandatory if value > Rs.100 (Registration Act S.17).
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Distinguish release vs gift vs sale vs partition — substance determines stamp duty + tax. Concessional rates for release to family co-sharer in many states.

promptInstructions: Draft a RELEASE / RELINQUISHMENT DEED. A release deed is an instrument by which a person (the releasor) gives up his/her right, title or interest in property in favour of another person (the releasee), who is typically an existing co-sharer / co-owner.

SUBSTANCE OVER FORM — courts and revenue authorities look at SUBSTANCE:
   (a) If releasee is a CO-SHARER / CO-OWNER and release is WITHOUT consideration — treated as RELEASE (lower stamp duty) — share simply enlarges the co-sharer's existing right.
   (b) If releasee is a CO-SHARER and release is WITH CONSIDERATION — may be treated as partial PARTITION or SALE; higher stamp duty.
   (c) If releasee is NOT a co-sharer (i.e., acquires fresh title via this deed) — treated as GIFT (if no consideration) or SALE (if consideration) — full stamp duty applies.
   (d) If RELEASE OF MORTGAGE by mortgagee to mortgagor — treated as RECONVEYANCE; separate stamp article.

STATE-WISE CONCESSIONS for release among family co-sharers (verify current rates):
   - Bihar: Article 55 — Rs.100 for release among co-sharers in family; otherwise sale rate.
   - Jharkhand: similar.
   - UP: Rs.5000 for release among family co-sharers (per state circular); otherwise full conveyance rate.
   - Delhi: 2% on value of released share for family co-sharer; up to 6% for non-family.
   DO NOT hardcode — flag advocate to verify.
STRUCTURE:
Para 1: Parties identification — Releasor + Releasee + Relationship.

Para 2: Recital of co-ownership — describe how releasor came to be co-owner. Examples:
   (a) Inheritance: 'The Releasor and Releasee are both Class I legal heirs of late [name], who died intestate on [date] leaving behind the immovable property described in Schedule A. The Releasor and Releasee, along with [other heirs if any], became co-owners of the said property by intestate succession under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.'
   (b) Partition: 'Pursuant to the Partition Deed dated [date] registered as [details], the Releasor and Releasee were allotted joint share in the property described in Schedule A.'
   (c) Joint purchase: 'By Sale Deed dated [date] registered as [details], the Releasor and Releasee jointly purchased the property described in Schedule A in equal/specified shares.'
   (d) Hindu Joint Family: 'The Releasor and Releasee are coparceners in the joint family property described in Schedule A.'
Para 3: Description of Share — '...the Releasor has a [fractional / percentage] share, namely [share], in the property described in Schedule A.'

Para 4: Motive / Recital of Family Settlement — 'Out of natural love and affection for the Releasee [who is the brother/sister/spouse/child] of the Releasor, AND/OR in furtherance of a family settlement / family arrangement, AND/OR for consideration of Rs. [amount] paid by the Releasee, the Releasor is desirous of relinquishing his/her share in favour of the Releasee.'

Para 5: OPERATIVE RELEASE CLAUSE — 'NOW THIS DEED WITNESSES that the Releasor doth hereby RELEASE, RELINQUISH, QUIT-CLAIM and ABANDON all his/her rights, title, interest, claim and demand whatsoever in respect of the [share] in the property described in Schedule A, in favour of the Releasee absolutely and forever; AND the Releasor doth hereby covenant that he/she shall have no manner of right, title or interest whatsoever in the said share hereafter.'
Para 6: Consideration clause (if applicable) — 'In consideration of the sum of Rs. [amount] paid by the Releasee to the Releasor (the receipt whereof Releasor hereby acknowledges)...'.

Para 7: NO FURTHER CLAIM — 'The Releasor covenants for himself, his heirs, executors, administrators and assigns, that he and they shall not, at any time hereafter, claim any right, title or interest in the released share, and that the Releasee shall hold, enjoy and dispose of the said share absolutely.'

Para 8: Warranty of title in released share — 'The Releasor warrants that he has good and marketable title in the released share, that the share is free from any encumbrance, mortgage, attachment or court order, and that no other person has any claim through the Releasor.'
Para 9: MUTATION AUTHORISATION — Releasor authorises Releasee to seek mutation in revenue / municipal records.
Para 10: INDEMNITY — Releasor indemnifies Releasee against any disturbance of title through Releasor or his heirs.
Para 11: Stamp duty + registration — borne by [specified party, usually Releasee].
Para 12: Schedule A — property description + share description.
Para 13: Witnesses (2 adults).
Append Lawie disclaimer.
Cite Kuppuswami Chettiar v. ASPA Arumugam Chettiar (1967) 1 SCR 275 — release operates by way of enlargement of existing co-sharer's right, not as fresh transfer.

Cite Kale v. Deputy Director of Consolidation (1976) 3 SCC 119 — family settlements (which often include releases) are indulgently treated by courts; bona fide settlements upheld even if technically defective.

Income tax: where release is treated as gift between relatives (S.56(2)(x) ITA definition of relative) — no tax in releasee's hands; if among non-relatives and value > Rs.50,000, taxable. Where release is treated as sale — capital gains for releasor.
Where releasor is a minor or under guardianship — additional flags; court permission for transfer of minor's interest required.

Note: For RELEASE OF MORTGAGE specifically (mortgagee releasing security to mortgagor on full payment) — different template — typically called RECONVEYANCE DEED or NO DUE / RELEASE OF MORTGAGE. Flag if user data shows mortgagee as releasor.

filing_checklist: Stamp paper per state Article 55 — concessional for family co-sharer release; full rate for non-co-sharer release
Original title documents demonstrating joint co-ownership / inheritance (succession certificate / family register)
Pedigree certificate / family tree from Tehsildar (for inheritance-based co-ownership)
PAN + Aadhaar of releasor and releasee
Relationship proof (where claiming family concession) — birth certificate / school records
Two adult witnesses with ID proofs
Both parties physically present at Sub-Registrar
Where releasor is minor — natural guardian's ID + court order under HMG Act
Where releasee is unrelated — flag higher stamp duty + gift tax / capital gains implications
Where release of mortgage — appropriate reconveyance template
Registration within 4 months of execution (S.23 Registration Act)
Post-registration: mutation in releasee's name only (releasor's name removed)
validation_rules: releasor_age >= 18 (otherwise flag minor + need court permission)
